no test skipped or deleted."

`__tests__/pipe-grep.test.ts` did not exist (verified: `git log --all` and
`git ls-tree` on `main` show the file was never present; the repo splits pipe
coverage into `pipe-grep-*.test.ts` files and AGENTS.md's hot-file rule directs
new pipe cases into a dedicated file). The change therefore creates
`__tests__/pipe-grep.test.ts`, a self-contained end-to-end test that runs real
ripgrep through both `ashlr__grep` and `ctx.grep` inside `ashlr__pipe` with
seven search terms (`TODO`, `café`, `café`, `日本語`, `🚀`,
`مرحبا`, `안녕하세요`) and asserts:

- Every matched `path:line:text` line preserves its Unicode text byte-exact
  (NFC `café`, decomposed `café`, CJK, emoji, Arabic with Eastern
  Arabic digits).
- NFC and NFD patterns stay distinct — `café` matches only the NFC line,
  `café` only the decomposed one; nothing is normalized.
- Piped output is byte-identical to the direct `ashlr__grep` result
  (pipe transparency).
- A Unicode term with zero hits still yields `[no matches]`; non-matching
  lines never leak.
- The spawned process forbids network access (`fetch` throws; `fetchCalls`
  must be 0) and runs with an isolated `HOME`/`ASHLR_HOME_OVERRIDE`.

Unambiguous `\u0301` escapes are used for the decomposed literals, matching
the convention in `__tests__/pipe-server-grep-unicode.test.ts`.

No source files were modified; no test was skipped or deleted.

## Summary

Task: test a literal replacement containing `` $` `` (JS's "text before the
match" token) in `__tests__/search-replace-regex.test.ts`. Acceptance: the
replacement is inserted literally; existing tests pass; no test skipped or
deleted.

`applyRegex` in `servers/search-replace-regex-server.ts` evaluates each
replacement via `m[0].replace(singleRe, replacement)` — against the match
substring alone — so a bare `` $` `` resolves to the empty string (nothing
precedes the match inside the match substring), while `$$` + backtick yields
the literal two characters `` $` ``. The new tests pin down both behaviors,
mirroring the existing `$'`/`$&` coverage.

Changes (all in `__tests__/search-replace-regex.test.ts`, purely additive):

- Header docstring now lists the `` $` `` coverage alongside the `$'`/`$&`
  entries.
- New test `literal replacement containing $` lands verbatim beside an
  expanding whole-match token`: `$$`=$&` writes `` $`=MARK `` at each of 3
  matches — literal `` $` `` plus an expanding `$&` prove the escape is
  honored without disabling tokens. Covered via dry run (bytes unchanged),
  apply (byte counts checked), and the tool handler JSON path.
- New test `literal replacement containing $` is written without inserting
  the preceding input`: a bare `` $` `` resolves to "" per match (prefixes
  "say "/"last " stay in place, never duplicated), then `$$`ok re-verified
  to land `` $` `` verbatim on disk.
- New `applyRegex` unit test `scopes $` expansion to the match substring —

body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-FLEETSOURCEQ8` (pool: devin), single commit on base `0a3fdc5fa`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-FLEETSOURCEQ8 — Bridge Notes

## Summary

The workbench was blind: `ashlr__fleet_state` read only `~/.ashlr/fleet/{targets.json,holds.json,jobs.jsonl,leader-events.jsonl}`, files the router no longer writes. Added `servers/_fleet-source.ts`, a read-only adapter that maps the live `~/.ashlr-runs` router queue to the existing `fleetState` shape:

- `queue/slots.json` → `targets` (lanes)
- `HOLD` → `holds`: a queue sentinel — absent means no hold (`{}`, never an error); JSON objects pass through as per-lane reasons; a JSON string list holds those lanes; any other content (or an empty file) is the hold reason applied to every lane in `slots.json` (`"*"` when lanes are unknown); a present-but-unreadable sentinel fails closed (lanes report `held` plus an error entry)
- `metrics/jobs.jsonl` → `jobs` (strict JSONL, last 20, same contract as before)
- `queue/dispatch-events.log` → `leader_event` (JSON records or `[timestamp] type job=X` text; tolerant of bad lines — the last parseable event wins, bad lines flag `invalid`)

`fleetState(root, runsRoot)` delegates to `fleetSource` only when **every** fleet file is missing, so the old layout stays authoritative whenever it exists. `runsRoot` defaults to the sibling `~/.ashlr-runs` of the injected fleet root, keeping fixture-rooted callers hermetic. `errors` keeps the canonical fleet file keys regardless of which layout served the read, so all downstream guards (`lanes`, `snapshot`, `session`) work unchanged.

Also wired the full-log readers through `readFleetJobsText` (`jobs.jsonl` → `metrics/jobs.jsonl` on ENOENT) so `fleet-steer lanes`, `fleet-snapshot` job upserts, `fleet-steer propose` observed lanes, and `ashlr__fleet_session` job records all see live router data when the fleet log is gone. Fixed a latent mislabel where a missing job log was reported `invalid` instead of `missing`.

Shared the hardened bounded read (`readBoundedText`) between both readers — same lstat/open/fstat, nofollow, single-link, traversal and 4 MiB guarantees; `readFleetText`/`readRunsText` keep their own fixed-name allowlists.

## Files

- `servers/_fleet-source.ts` — new read-only adapter (`readBoundedText`, `readRunsText`, `runsRootFor`, `fleetSource`)
- `servers/fleet-state-server-handlers.ts` — `readFleetJobsText`, runs fallback in `fleetState`, tool description
- `servers/fleet-session-server-handlers.ts` — jobs read via `readFleetJobsText`, description
- `servers/fleet-snapshot-server-handlers.ts` — description
- `scripts/fleet-steer.ts`, `scripts/fleet-snapshot.ts` — full-log reads via `readFleetJobsText`; ENOENT reported as `missing`
